title: Spec-Driven Development: Agentic Coding at FAANG Scale and Quality — Al Harris, Amazon Kiro
summary: Kiro's Al Harris (AI Engineer) on spec-driven development: EARS requirements, design, tasks, property-based tests, MCP and steering, prompt bias.

assertions.quote: you give us a prompt and we will take that and turn it into a set of clear requirements with acceptance criteria

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: We represent these acceptance criteria in the EARS format

verdicts.note: Checkable acceptance criteria give agents a stopping condition and give reviewers a test; out-of-scope lists reduce scope creep. Standard practice that carries over well to agents.

The review interprets vibe coding as productive when the evaluation loop is systematic 'with defined acceptance criteria, automated testing, and structured prompt refinement'; this is interpretive, not tested.

assertions.quote: your ears requirements can be translated directly into properties of the system which are effectively invariants

verdicts.note: Property-based testing is a strong verification technique and pairs well with explicit invariants; vendor-reported gains, and property quality still depends on how well they're written.

assertions.quote: the LLMs are very good at saying I'm done. I'm happy ... Oh, yeah. The tests don't pass but they're annoying

verdicts.note: Widely reported and seen in evals: agents claim tests pass or features are complete when they aren't; reading summaries critically is necessary.

assertions.quote: Anything you put in the prompt is effectively rounding the agent. For better or for worse

verdicts.note: LLMs are known to be sycophantic and anchor on user suggestions; prompting for alternatives or critique reliably surfaces other options.

assertions.quote: the agent ... does better when given less context but given the tools to understand where to go find things

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: if your system already had good separation of concerns ... it's going to have a great job

verdicts.note: Clear module boundaries help both humans and agents navigate and test; consistent with Ousterhout and practitioner reports.

assertions.quote: It is like this living documentation about the system

verdicts.note: Specs help align agents, but code is still what runs; specs drift from implementation unless continuously maintained, and practitioners like Pocock report specs-only workflows failing.

assertions.quote: once I go through that pain of learning I just say kira write what you learned into a steering doc

verdicts.note: Encoding lessons in rules and workflows does reduce repeat mistakes, but rule files bloat and conflict if not pruned; gains are real but not automatically compounding.
